parts: [{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is a Secretariat?","marks":1,"answer":"Generally, the collective term for various ministries and their departmental offices is the Secretariat.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Why is the President of Bangladesh referred to as the procedural (ceremonial) head? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Since Bangladesh follows a parliamentary democratic system, the President is called the procedural (ceremonial) head. According to the Constitution, he is the Head of State. However, he does not exercise any executive power. Although all republican activities are constitutionally conducted in his name, executive authority is vested in the Prime Minister and the Cabinet. For this reason, he is known as the procedural head.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Which local organization is Mr. 'B' a member of? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"Mr. 'B' is a member of a Union Parishad. The Union Parishad is a vital body of local government in Bangladesh. It operates on the basis of public representation to establish local governance in rural areas. It is the oldest local institution in the country. The organization consists of one elected Chairman, nine elected members, and three reserved seats for women members. In total, including the Chairman, there are 13 members. The organization primarily maintains peace and order, prevents crime, resolves family and social disputes, and prevents riots in rural areas. Therefore, Mr. 'B' is a member of the Union Parishad.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"\"Mr. 'A's institution plays a crucial role in implementing central decisions at the local level.\" Do you agree with this statement? Provide arguments.","marks":4,"answer":"Yes, I agree that Mr. 'A's institution, the District Administration, plays an indispensable role in implementing central decisions at the local level. The third tier of Bangladesh's administrative structure is the District Administration. The head of the District Administration is the Deputy Commissioner (DC). He is an experienced member of the Bangladesh Civil Service. As stated, Mr. 'A' is an experienced civil servant and heads a unit at the third tier, meaning his institution is the District Administration. There is a direct link between the central government and the district administration. All decisions related to districts taken at the Bangladesh Secretariat are sent directly to the Deputy Commissioner. The DC manages district administration according to central directives. In other words, the District Administration plays a crucial role in implementing policies, decisions, and programs from the Secretariat at the Upazila and Union levels. It supervises, coordinates, and controls all internal district activities. Based on the above discussion, it can be concluded that Mr. 'A's institution (District Administration) plays a highly significant role in implementing central decisions locally.\n","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts: [{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is a Secretariat?","marks":1,"answer":"The collective term for various ministries and their departmental offices is the Secretariat.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Explain the role of political parties in a democratic system.","marks":2,"answer":"The role of political parties in a democratic system is extremely important. The existence of strong, well-organized political parties is a primary condition for the success of a democratic government. Modern democratic governance is essentially the governance of political parties. Political parties identify various political, social, and economic issues in the country and formulate party policies and programs accordingly. To win elections, they publicize programs and generate public support. After winning, they form the government and rule the country. Hence, political parties are indispensable and crucial in a democracy.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Which local institution is Mr. Rayhan the head of? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"Mr. Rayhan is the Chairman of a Union Parishad. The Union Parishad is the oldest local government institution in Bangladesh. It is typically formed with around 10-15 villages. It consists of one elected Chairman, nine elected members, and three reserved seats for women members (12 members in total excluding the Chairman). The Union Parishad resolves disputes, prevents crime, carries out welfare activities, and maintains peace and order in the union. The description in the stem matches the Union Parishad's composition and functions. Therefore, Mr. Rayhan is the Chairman of the Union Parishad.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Which government branch resembles Mr. Rahman's organization? Is that organization the only source of law? Provide arguments in support of your answer.","marks":4,"answer":"Mr. Rahman's organization resembles the Legislative branch or Legislature. However, the Legislature is not the only source of law. One of the three branches of government is the Legislature, which enacts and amends laws as needed. Mr. Rahman is an elected member of this law-making body. In a modern state, the Legislature is the primary source of law, but other sources also exist, such as customs, religion and religious texts, judicial decisions (case law), juristic writings, and principles of equity and justice. Nevertheless, considering public interest and the need for formal legislation, the Legislature remains the primary source in a modern state. Therefore, it is not the sole source of law.\n","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts: [{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is the name of Bangladesh's legislature?","marks":1,"answer":"The name of Bangladesh's legislature is the Jatiya Sangsad (National Parliament).","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Why is the Secretariat called the nerve center of the administrative system?","marks":2,"answer":"Since all government decisions are first taken at the Secretariat, it is called the nerve center of the administrative system. The Secretariat is located at the core of Bangladesh's administrative structure and acts as the brain of governance. Decisions taken here flow step-by-step to the Division, District Administration, and Upazila Administration. Thus, it sits at the center of administration. All departments, offices, and government bodies are accountable to the Secretariat.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Which important organ does Image-1 indicate? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"Image-1 indicates the District Administration. The District Administration implements all administrative decisions and policies formulated by the Bangladesh Secretariat. Key functions include supervising departmental activities, providing public services, promoting education and culture, and maintaining law and order in the district. Additionally, constructing and maintaining roads, improving public health, expanding education, establishing small industries, and supporting sports and cultural activities are notable tasks. The Deputy Commissioner oversees administration, revenue, local governance, judicial functions, and all district activities, ensuring good governance and public welfare. The tasks shown in Image-1 involve routine government work, implementing national decisions, and maintaining law and order, which fall under the District Administration.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Do you think the duties mentioned in Image-2 are sufficient for a local self-governing institution? Provide arguments in support of your answer.","marks":4,"answer":"The local self-governing institution in Image-2 is the Municipality (Pourashava). The duties listed are not sufficient for a Municipality. A Municipality addresses urban problems, undertakes development activities, and works based on area-specific planning. Essential tasks include planning and constructing city roads, highways, and residential areas, ensuring public safety, contributing to healthcare, and establishing welfare centers. In cities, high population density leads to family and social disputes, and resolving these is also a municipal function. Image-2 only mentions road/residential planning and establishing mother-and-child centers, covering planning, public safety, and health. It omits other critical duties like pure water supply, drainage, road maintenance, tree plantation, scholarships for poor and meritorious students, social welfare, and arbitration. Given the Municipality's broad mandate to solve urban problems and drive development, the listed duties are insufficient. Therefore, the Municipality must perform many more tasks for public welfare.\n","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts: [{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is local administration?","marks":1,"answer":"Local administration refers to the governance system operating at the divisional, district, and upazila levels.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Why is the Secretariat called the nerve center of the administrative system? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"The Bangladesh Secretariat is the focal point of the country's administrative structure and serves as the nerve center of administration. It makes all major administrative decisions. It comprises several ministries, each under a respective minister. The executive and administrative powers of a ministry are vested in the Secretary.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"In which branch does Mr. Azmal work? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"Mr. Azmal works in the Judiciary. The Judiciary is one of the three branches of the Bangladesh government. It establishes justice in society, protects citizens' personal liberty and fundamental rights, and impartially safeguards public rights. The description of his branch aligns with the Judiciary. Ensuring equal rights and good governance for all citizens requires the rule of law. The Judiciary's duty is to ensure justice according to law and protect fundamental rights. Without an independent judiciary, the state administration could deprive citizens of their rights, influential criminals might evade punishment, public trust in law would decline, and social disorder would rise. Therefore, ensuring the rule of law is essential for good governance. The rule of law is effectively implemented through fair, impartial judicial proceedings and punishing offenders according to law.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"\"Mr. Arman's branch controls Mr. Rafik's branch.\" – Analyze this statement.","marks":4,"answer":"[Corrected for factual accuracy] The statement is incorrect. In the stem, Mr. Arman is a district administrative head, representing the Executive Branch. Mr. Rafik is an elected representative from seat 'K', representing the Legislature (Parliament). In a parliamentary democratic system, the Legislature controls the Executive, not the other way around. The Parliament exercises control over the Executive through questioning, debates, scrutinizing administrative performance, and approving budgets. The Prime Minister and Cabinet are accountable to Parliament. Parliament can pass adjournment motions, censures, or no-confidence motions against ministers. If the government loses parliamentary confidence, it must resign. While the Executive implements laws and policies, many crucial administrative actions require legislative approval. Therefore, Mr. Rafik's branch (Legislature) controls Mr. Arman's branch (Executive), making the original statement factually inaccurate.\n","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts: [{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is the term of the Parliament?","marks":1,"answer":"The term of the Parliament is 5 years.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Why is forest land gradually decreasing?","marks":2,"answer":"Forest land is gradually decreasing due to population growth, deforestation, and other factors. Rising population increases demand for fuel, timber, and other necessities, leading to tree cutting. Additionally, industrialization and urbanization increase the demand for forest wood as raw materials, putting continuous pressure on forests. Consequently, forest land is shrinking.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Which river in your textbook is indicated by river 'C'? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"The river 'C' mentioned is the Karnaphuli River. It is the main river in the southeastern region of Bangladesh. It originates from the Lushai Hills in Mizoram, India. Stretching 320 km, it flows through Chittagong city and the Chittagong Hill Tracts, making it the most important river in the region. It enters Bangladesh through Rangamati district, with 180 km flowing through India's hilly regions. It splits into two main branches at Dhuliahchhari and Kaptai. It then flows through the Sitaram Hill range to Chandraghona, passes through the Chittagong plains, and empties into the Bay of Bengal. Its main tributaries include Kaptai, Halda, Kasalong, and Rangkhiang. Rafik lives on its bank. A dam was built on it to establish a hydroelectric power plant, making it vital for trade and commerce in the Chittagong region. Therefore, river 'C' refers to the Karnaphuli.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"The work done by Mr. Amjad for water and food security was beneficial for his local people. – Evaluate this.","marks":4,"answer":"Mr. Amjad's efforts to ensure water and food security were indeed beneficial for his local community. The Union Parishad Chairman is responsible for informing the public about government and NGO services in agriculture, health, fisheries, livestock, and education, as well as implementing projects for rural infrastructure development, poverty alleviation, sanitation, water supply, drainage, and welfare activities. Additionally, distributing improved seeds, saplings, and fertilizers to farmers, promoting rural industries, advising on income-generating activities, and creating employment are his duties. In Event-2, Chairman Amjad ensures continuous water supply and raises awareness against water wastage. This is a welfare-oriented activity. It ensures necessary irrigation water during dry seasons, boosts agricultural production, reduces the national food deficit, and decreases dependency on food imports. Therefore, as Union Parishad Chairman, Mr. Amjad's work is highly significant and beneficial for his locality.\n","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts: [{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is the Executive Branch?","marks":1,"answer":"The Executive Branch is the government division responsible for conducting administrative and governmental work, maintaining law and order, and implementing the state's overall decisions and facilities.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Why is local self-governance important? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Local self-governance is of immense importance. Modern states are vast in population and area, making it impossible for the central government in the capital to smoothly administer the entire country, effectively solve local problems, take timely measures, and ensure balanced development alone. Local self-governance makes this easier. Moreover, it enables public participation in governance and development, raises awareness, builds leadership, and ensures administrative transparency and accountability. Hence, it is indispensable.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Which government official's work resembles Mr. 'X's work? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"Mr. 'X's work resembles that of an Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) or Deputy Commissioner (DC). District Administration is the third tier of Bangladesh's administrative structure. The DC is the central figure of district administration, an experienced civil servant, and a senior administrative officer positioned after the Divisional Commissioner. He manages district administration according to central directives and is accountable to the Divisional Commissioner. As the chief revenue collector, he collects land revenue and other taxes, coordinates with all government departments in the district, and handles various judicial and administrative duties, including disaster relief. Therefore, Mr. 'X' is a Deputy Commissioner or UNO.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"\"Mr. 'Y's work is not limited to what is mentioned in Event-2.\" Do you agree with this statement? Provide arguments in support of your opinion.","marks":4,"answer":"Mr. 'Y' represents the Prime Minister. I agree that his duties are not limited to those in Event-2. As head of the government, the Prime Minister is directly elected by the people (through their representatives). The President appoints the leader of the majority party in Parliament as Prime Minister, around whom the governance system revolves. He is the chief executive, leader of the Parliament, and head of the Cabinet, which he forms at his discretion. He can dismiss any minister. His resignation or loss of parliamentary confidence leads to the government's fall. Beyond international representation and rule-making, he coordinates all state activities, oversees all ministries, divisions, and departments, and guides policy on justice, economy, foreign affairs, and governance. He is the central figure of the administration and the true leader and guide of the nation. Therefore, his responsibilities extend far beyond the stated tasks.\n","image":null,"image_url":null}]

He forms and leads the cabinet, remains in power as long as he retains parliamentary majority, and his resignation triggers the resignation of all ministers. As leader of Parliament and his political party, he advises the President on appointments, policies, and governance. He coordinates national security, unity, and all administrative functions. It appoints and manages chowkidars and dafadars, acts as a salish (arbitration) court to resolve disputes peacefully, distributes improved seeds/fertilizers/pesticides for agriculture, promotes cooperatives and cottage industries, advises on income-generating activities, and manages village police and volunteer forces.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"In the context of Bangladesh, what role does the mentioned local government play in ensuring proper services to rural people? Explain with practical information.","marks":4,"answer":"The Union Parishad ensures proper services to rural people through various activities. It informs the public about government/NGO services in agriculture, health, fisheries, livestock, and education; implements projects for rural infrastructure, poverty alleviation, sanitation, water supply, and drainage; distributes improved agricultural inputs; promotes rural industries; advises on income generation; and creates employment. It also constructs/maintains roads, assists widows/orphans/poor, establishes primary healthcare centers, supervises primary education, conserves the environment, establishes libraries/parks/playgrounds, manages disasters and relief, maintains government property (roads, bridges, canals, power/telecom lines), and promotes rural electrification. Through these comprehensive activities, the Union Parishad effectively ensures rural public welfare and development.\n","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts: [{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is the Legislature?","marks":1,"answer":"The Legislature is the government branch responsible for creating new laws, amending, expanding, and modifying existing laws for the country.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Explain the judicial powers of the Parliament.","marks":2,"answer":"The Jatiya Sangsad (National Parliament) is Bangladesh's Legislature. Beyond lawmaking, it exercises judicial powers, including legal oversight, controlling the Executive, and financial supervision. It can impeach the President and remove the Speaker, Deputy Speaker, and Ombudsman if necessary, according to the Constitution.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Which position in the Bangladesh government does 'X' indicate in the question? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"'X' indicates the President. He holds the highest ceremonial position and is the Head of State. He exercises all duties and powers granted by the Constitution and laws. He assents to bills passed by Parliament, which become law within 15 days of his approval. As supreme commander of the defense forces, he safeguards national sovereignty. The stem mentions parliamentary powers, ordinance issuance, and appointment powers, which align with the President's constitutional role.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"\"The position indicated by 'X' is not limited to the mentioned duties only.\" – Provide arguments based on your textbook.","marks":4,"answer":"The President's duties are not limited to those listed. In a parliamentary system, he is the ceremonial head. All executive actions are conducted in his name, though he lacks independent executive power. He plays crucial roles in government formation, governance, lawmaking, finance, defense, and diplomacy. Beyond assenting to bills and issuing ordinances, he appoints the PM, judges, and constitutional officials (on PM's advice), convenes Parliament, delivers addresses, prorogues/dissolves Parliament on PM's advice, and serves as supreme commander of defense forces. He also recommends money bills and can pardon sentences. Thus, his constitutional and ceremonial roles extend far beyond the listed tasks.\n","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts: [{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is government in a general sense?","marks":1,"answer":"In a general sense, government refers to all administrators who directly or indirectly participate in state governance.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Explain \"declaration of a state of emergency\".","marks":2,"answer":"According to Article 141A(1) of the Constitution, the President may declare a state of emergency if satisfied that Bangladesh or any part thereof is threatened by war, external aggression, or internal disturbance, endangering security or economic life. However, prior approval of the Prime Minister is required for its validity. During an emergency, certain constitutional provisions and fundamental rights may be suspended as specified.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"What is the name of (C)? Explain its main functions.","marks":3,"answer":"'C' is the Judiciary, which plays a crucial role in establishing justice and protecting citizens' personal liberty. Its functions include trying accused individuals, interpreting laws, protecting fundamental rights, safeguarding the Constitution, and advising the administration on legal matters.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"(B) establishes control over (A) – Prove this statement.","marks":4,"answer":"Organ 'B' is the Legislature, and organ 'A' is the Executive Branch. The Legislature controls the Executive. In a parliamentary system, the Executive is accountable to the Legislature. Parliament exercises control through questions, debates, budget approvals, no-confidence motions, and scrutiny of administrative performance. The Prime Minister and Cabinet must answer to Parliament. If the government loses parliamentary confidence, it must resign. Many executive actions require legislative approval. Thus, the Legislature effectively controls the Executive to ensure democratic accountability.\n","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts: [{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is the name of the legislature in most Islamic countries?","marks":1,"answer":"The legislature in most Islamic countries is called the Majlis or Shura.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"What do you understand by local self-governance?","marks":2,"answer":"Local self-governance refers to self-rule by the people in a specific area, managed by elected representatives who are accountable to the public. Key features include: legal basis, elected bodies, public participation in decision-making, capacity to raise funds through taxation, diverse functions, planning authority, and autonomy from higher government interference.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Explain the background of the formation of the local government institution mentioned in the question.","marks":3,"answer":"The mentioned institution is the Union Parishad. It is the oldest local organization in Bangladesh. Its evolution dates back to the British era: the Chowkidari Act of 1870 established a 5-member body for law and order. The Bengal Local Act of 1885 created Union Committees, Subdivisional Boards, and District Boards. The Village Act of 1919 replaced these with a Union Board. During Pakistan, it was renamed Union Council. After Bangladesh's independence, the Local Government Ordinance established the three-tier system, with the Union Parishad as the grassroots foundation for simplified local administration.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"\"Are the mentioned duties the only functions of this institution?\" – Provide arguments in support of your answer.","marks":4,"answer":"No, these are not the only duties. The Union Parishad has numerous other important functions. Ensuring village security, appointing chowkidars/dafadars, preventing crime/smuggling, supervising secretaries and staff are key tasks. It also constructs/maintains roads, assists widows/orphans/poor, provides primary healthcare, supervises primary education, protects the environment, maintains cleanliness, manages disaster relief, maintains government infrastructure, and promotes rural electrification. These administrative and voluntary activities go far beyond agricultural input distribution, proving that the institution's mandate is comprehensive.\n","image":null,"image_url":null}]
